newsitem.title: GREECE: PASOK'S ROMEOS BLASTS REVISION OF GREEK CONVERGENCE PLAN.
newsitem.headline: PASOK'S ROMEOS BLASTS REVISION OF GREEK CONVERGENCE PLAN.

text.p: The revision of Greece's convergence plan with the European Union proposed by the conservative New Democracy party is unlikely to be approved by the EU and will stall Greek economic growth, Deputy Foreign Minister George Romeos told Reuters.
"We do not think that a revision of the convergence plan is likely," said Romeos.

"It must be pointed out that a revision has to be justified to be approved by the EU commission and the process is time consuming. It will undermine our efforts to stabilise the economy and speed up growth," he said.

Greece has submitted two convergence plans to the European Union which have both been approved by the European Commission. The current revised convergence plan was given the green light in 1994 after a previous one was scrapped as unattainable.

"We (PASOK) insist on the implementation of the convergence plan because it is in line with the Greek economy's potential. Our goal is to meet the Maastricht targets on time and enter our country into EMU," said Romeos.

He added that the performance of the Greek economy has been better than projected in the convergence plan in a number of macroeconomic areas and expressed optimism that Greece will be present in the third phase of the EMU.

"Current macroeconomic fundamentals make me optimistic that Greece will participate in the third phase of EMU," he said. "Official figures by the OECD and the European Commission that Reuters has carried justify this optimism." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
